title: Senior Leader Cutterhead Dredge Forum
description: On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Senior Leader Cutterhead Dredge Forum will provide a platform for collaboration focused on challenges and opportunities in the cutterhead dredging industry. This forum is open to all cutterhead dredging companies that are currently performing business in the New Orleans District or are interested in doing so. The dredge forum will provide an opportunity for dredging industry leaders to meet with USACE senior leaders and technical personnel to discuss New Orleans District dredging projects and funding. There will be two (2) attendee slots (leadership positions) available per company. If your company is interested in attending, please complete one registration form for each company and submit no later than October 16, 2026. Should an attendee/company have a question they would like to be discussed at the forum, please submit the inquiries via email to Yojna Calix at Yojna.Calix@usace.army.mil and Ashley Wainright at Ashley.Wainright@usace.army.mil, no later than 25 September 2026. Time: 9:00am - 12:00pm (CST) Location: USACE New Orleans District Headquarters District Assembly Room (DARM) 7400 Leake Avenue New Orleans, LA 70118 This event is free of charge. All attendees will be required to Pre-register for the event for attendance and to gain access to the installation. Each company should submit one registration with both attendees� information. Furthermore, information about the company's cutterhead dredges, as well as dredging experience in the last three years, will be a part of the registration submittal and must be completed. TO REGISTER: Please register at: https://form.jotform.com/251965714470159 The acquisition forecast information does not represent a pre-solicitation notice or a Request for Quotation/Proposal and is not a commitment by the Government to purchase products or services. We look forward to meeting with you.

title: F108--Radioactive Waste Removal and Disposal Services
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice for Radioactive Waste Removal & Disposal Services as identified in the Statement of Work (SOW) for the Ann Arbor VA Medical Center in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The contractor shall furnish all necessary tools, parts, labor, supplies, materials, equipment, supervision and transportation necessary to furnish the services noted below. A DRAFT SOW is attached to this notice and is subject to change should a solicitation be issued as a result of this notice. Please respond if you have the ability and actual intention to complete this requirement. All of the following information is required in your response: SAM UEI NUMBER provide this in the email text GSA Contract Number provide this in the email text Capabilities Statement Confirmation of actual intent to submit an offer should an RFQ be posted in future Company name and address Point of contact information (name, phone, email) Socioeconomic size status (example: large business, small business, WOSB, SDVOSB, etc.) provide this in the email text This Sources Sought Notice is intended to locate any business capable of performance. The anticipated NAICS Code for this requirement is 562211. This is not a Request for Quotation and quotes shall not be reviewed at this time. The Government shall not be responsible for any costs incurred by the contractor because of this Sources Sought Notice. This notice shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to ultimately award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government to any particular acquisition approach. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary; the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Responses shall be submitted to Jeanne Ortiz at jeanne.ortiz@va.gov by Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET). Responses MUST include 36C25027Q0045 in the subject line. PHONE CALLS SHALL NOT BE ACCEPTED FOR THIS NOTICE. DRAFT STATEMENT OF WORK Part I: General Information Introduction The Department of Veterans Affairs Ann Arbor Health Care System (VAAAHS) has a requirement for commercial radioactive waste removal for final disposition of liquid and solid uniform radioactive Low-Level Waste (LLW) to be completed by a qualified contractor in accordance with Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) regulations outlined in 10 CFR 20, 10 CFR 30, 10 CFR 40, 10 CFR 61 and 10 CFR 71 as well as all applicable United States Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations outlined in 49 CFR, and any applicable Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) regulations for required training, handling, packaging, labeling, placarding, transporting, and final disposition. Timely disposal of radioactive waste requires a vender with NRC licenses for treatment and disposal of radioactive and radioactive mixed hazardous waste (mixed waste). A successful bidder shall have Department of Transportation (DOT) registration for transportation of hazardous materials and personnel who are certified as being trained for handling, packaging, and shipping radioactive and mixed hazardous waste. Failure to manage radioactive waste including timely treatment and disposal could result in regulatory violations, fines, and/or the revocation of the VAAAHS permit to use radioactive material under the Department of Veterans Affairs Master Materials Licenses issued by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The VAAAHS system has two locations in which radioactive LLW will be picked up, 2215 Fuller Road, Ann Arbor, Michigan and 1200 South Detroit Avenue, Toledo, Ohio. Part II: Requirements Qualifications and Responsibilities of Contacted Personnel: A qualified contactor must have an active Radioactive Materials License granted by the NRC or an Agreement State to be able to handle, possess and dispose of the radioactive waste outlined in the next section. All transporters must maintain a current commercial driver s license (CDL) with a hazardous materials endorsement (H) to verify that the drivers possess the knowledge and skills necessary to handle and transport DOT class 7 radioactive materials. All applicable state and local permits must also be maintained by the contractor. All expenses associated with these qualifications are at the expense of the contractor and shall not be billed to the Federal Government. 2. Services to Be Performed: a. The contractor shall provide a current copy of their Radioactive Materials License as well as proof of transporter radiation safety training and CDLs. b. The contractor shall provide a template for both spent sealed sources and radioactive waste summary/inventory forms to be completed by the VAAAHS and submitted to the contractor prior to removal from the facility. There shall be no charge for this service. c. The contractor shall provide a current uniform low-level radioactive waste manifest (NRC Form 540 or equivalent substitute) that is to be filled out in its entirety and signed by both the contractor and the VAAAHS Radiation Safety Staff at the time of transfer of sealed sources and radioactive waste. There shall be no charge for this service. The waste manifest shall be compared against the sealed source and radioactive waste summary/inventory forms to ensure they match prior to transport away from the facility. Any discrepancies shall be resolved prior to transport. The contractor shall provide all required packaging such as boxes, pails, etc. for safe transportation of sealed sources and radioactive waste in accordance with NRC and DOT regulation. e. The Contractor shall take all necessary radioactive measurements and ensure that the packages are properly labeled in accordance with NRC and DOT regulations prior to transport. f. The contractor shall coordinate radioactive waste pick-up services with the VAAAHS Radiation Safety Staff. g. The Contractor shall remove the radioactive waste no less than once per contract year and not to exceed two pickups during the contract period: Any patient treatment waste byproduct material with Atomic Numbers 1-83, 88, and 89 in any form that includes unused radioactive unit dose vials (aqueous liquid) or patient radioactive waste (Biological/Sharps) not to exceed 50 pounds. Any byproduct material with Atomic Numbers 3-83 radioactive sealed sources or radioactive waste not to exceed 200 pounds. This includes sealed sources at locations of use and or unsealed radioactive waste generated. Scintillation Vials Liquid scintillation cocktail in vials containing byproduct material with Atomic Numbers 1-83, 88, and 89. Liquid Mixed Waste Radioactive waste containing EPA characteristic and/or listed hazardous material. This waste stream will be packaged in shipping containers according to waste profile requirements specified by the successful bidder. In accordance with 10 CFR Part 20 (Appendix G) a written notification that the contractor has received the radioactive shipments that were picked up from the VAAAHS must be provided to the VAAAHS Radiation Safety Staff. The NRC Form 540 or equivalent substitute must also be returned with item number 9 filled out with the contractor s signature acknowledging confirmation of the receipt of the radioactive waste. A final disposal certificate shall also be provided to the VAAAHS Radiation Safety Staff when final processing has been completed. The contractor shall be responsible for any leaks or spills that occur after taking possession of radioactive waste and spent sealed sources. Part III: Supporting Information Response Time Contractor shall respond by email within one week of when services are requested by email via the Ann Arbor VA Medical Center Radiation Safety Staff to schedule service with the Ann Arbor VA Medical Center Radiation Safety Staff. Contractor shall be on-site for service within three hours of the scheduled date/time unless there are unforeseeable circumstances that require rescheduling

title: 3PL Follow-on Effort RFI
description: The General Services Administration (GSA), Federal Acquisition Service (FAS), General Supplies and Services (GSS) Portfolio, Office of Supply Chain Management (SCM) and Internal and Emergency Acquisition Division (IEAD) has a requirement a Third Party Logistics (3PL) provider in support of export operations to support overseas customers. Historically, these customers had previously been serviced by GSA and Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) distribution centers.This effort includes receipt of inbound Transatlantic and Transpacific ocean shipments from multiple award schedule vendors, inspection and preparation for shipment of goods or containers to an intermediate destination, then to another destination, i.e. transshipment; as well as shipment consolidation, ensuring readiness for onward movement in accordance with required Department of Defense (DoD) and Federal regulations through small package carriers, the U.S. Postal System (USPS) and Defense Transportation System (DTS), and reporting on noted discrepancies. Requirement synopsis: This requirement is Export Operations Support through the use of a Third-Party Logistics (3PL) to better align GSA warehousing, cargo movement and distribution processes with industry standards and simplify disposal, hazardous movement, storage and distribution requirements. See Google link in RFI attachment for detailed questions.

title: Kompostitarkastusten hyvien käytäntöjen kehittämishankkeen hankinta
description: Kompostitarkastusten hyvien käytäntöjen kehittämishankkeen hankinta Hankinnan kohteena on Hankintayksikön Kompostitarkastusten hyvien käytäntöjen kehittämishankkeen hankinta. Tarkemmin hankinnan kohteena on asiantuntijapalvelu, jossa tehtävänä on laatia selvitys kompostitarkastusten nykytilasta sekä opas ja viestintämateriaalia kompostitarkastusten hyvistä käytännöistä. Hanke on tarkoitus toteuttaa yhteistyössä Suomen Kuntaliitto ry:n, kuntien jätehuoltoviranomaisten sekä tarvittavien muiden viranomaisten ja asiantuntijatahojen kanssa. Hankkeessa tulee lisäksi kuulla kotikompostointia harjoittavia asukkaita tarkoituksenmukaisella tavalla. Tiedonkeruussa voidaan hyödyntää esimerkiksi kyselyitä, haastatteluja ja työpajoja. Palveluntuottaja vastaa hankkeen suunnittelusta, toteutuksesta, sidosryhmäyhteistyöstä, aineiston analysoinnista, raportoinnista sekä hankkeessa tuotettavan oppaan ja muun viestintämateriaalin laatimisesta ja hankkeen tulosten esittelystä yleisö- ja sidosryhmätilaisuuksissa. Materiaali tuotetaan pääasiassa suomenkielisenä, mutta opas laaditaan myös ruotsiksi ja yleistajuinen viestintämateriaali myös ruotsiksi ja englanniksi. Ympäristöministeriö vastaa oppaan julkaisemisesta Ympäristöministeriön julkaisuja -sarjassa. Hankinnan kohteena oleva työ alkaa mahdollisimman pian hankintasopimuksen solmimisen jälkeen ja päättyy viimeistään 30.4.2027. Suomenkielisen oppaan ja viestintämateriaalien tulee olla valmiina viimeistään 31.3.2027. Valtakunnallinen info- tai verkkotilaisuus tulee toteuttaa viimeistään viikolla 14. Muiden tuotosten tulee olla valmiina tai toteutettuna viimeistään 30.4.2027. Tarjouksessa tulee esittää palvelun toteutuksesta vastaava asiantuntija (projektipäällikkö). Projektipäälliköllä tulee olla tukenaan palvelun toteutuksessa riittävä määrä muita asiantuntijoita. Hankintayksikkö on varannut toimeksiannon toteuttamiseen enintään 65 000 euroa (+mahdollinen alv). Hankinnan tarkempi kuvaus on liitteessä 1 (Palvelun kuvaus). Liitteessä 2 (CV-lomake) ilmoitetut hankinnan kohdetta koskevat vaatimukset ovat pakollisia vaatimuksia. Tarjottavan palvelun tulee täyttää kaikki palvelulle asetetut pakolliset vaatimukset, jotta sen voidaan katsoa olevan tarjouspyynnön mukainen. Hankintayksikkö valitsee yhden (1) toimittajan, jonka kanssa se tekee sopimuksen.,

Security Requirements The contractor employees shall not have access to VA sensitive or computer information and will not require routine access to VA Facilities. The contractor employees shall require intermittent access only and will be escorted by VA employees while at VA Facilities. No background investigation is required. Access to VA Information and Info Systems The contractor or subcontractor must notify the Contracting Officer immediately when an employee working on a VA system or with access to VA information is reassigned or leaves the contractor or subcontractor s employ. The Contracting Officer must also be notified immediately by the contractor or subcontractor prior to an unfriendly termination. Contract personnel who require access to national security programs must have a valid security clearance. National Industrial Security Program (NISP) was established by Executive Order 12829 to ensure that cleared U.S. defense industry contract personnel safeguard the classified information in their possession while performing work on contracts, programs, bids, or research and development efforts. The Department of Veterans Affairs does not have a Memorandum of Agreement with Defense Security Service (DSS). Verification of a Security Clearance must be processed through the Special Security Officer located in the Planning and National Security Service within the Office of Operations, Security, and Preparedness. Custom software development and outsourced operations must be located in the U.S. to the maximum extent practical. If such services are proposed to be performed abroad and are not disallowed by other VA policy or mandates, the contractor/subcontractor must state where all non-U.S. services are provided and detail a security plan, deemed to be acceptable by VA, specifically to address mitigation of the resulting problems of communication, control, data protection, and so forth. Location within the U.S. may be an evaluation factor. VA Information Custodial Language For service that involves the storage, generating, transmitting, or exchanging of VA sensitive information but does not require C&A or an MOU-ISA for system interconnection, the contractor/subcontractor must complete a Contractor Security Control Assessment (CSCA) on a yearly basis and provide it to the COTR. title: Airfield Blast Shield
description: Amendment 0001 (13 Oct 2026): The purpose of this amendment is to � Extend the Proposal Due Date to 27 October 2026. � All other solicitation requirements remain unchanged and in full effect. 1.1 PROJECT DESCRIPTION: 1.1.1 Work under this project shall consist of providing all plant, labor, equipment, appliances, materials, and performing all operations required to cover the fabrication and erection of new Blast Deflector Fences for the B1-B. All work shall comply with the contract specifications and shall be in accordance with the latest International Building Code (IBC), National Fire Codes, Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC), Engineering Technical Letters (ETL�s), and all applicable Federal, State and local regulations/codes. 2.1 GENERAL: 2.1.1 The blast deflector shall be of the curved, non-perforated, galvanized, corrugated type, with corrugations running in a horizontal direction. The Lynnco Type GS-20-2 as manufactured by Blast Deflectors, Inc shall be considered as the standard for this work. At the option of the Contracting Officer, alternate types of blast deflectors may be considered provided the drawings and specifications of alternate types are approved by Contracting Officer. The blast fence shall be furnished and installed by a manufacturer/contractor with blast fence experience. The blast fence shall be capable of withstanding the afterburner throttle at 30,000 lbs thrust of a B1-B Bomber engine nozzle 90 ft/ (min.) from front of deflector foundation. Extrapolated temperature is approx. 1400 ? velocity @ 900 MPH. 2.1.2 Haul Route: Approved haul route is from the Tye Gate, Third Street, Ave E, Second Street, to Flightline. Haul Route subject to change based on Flightline Restrictions. Contractors are required to use the Tye Gate for all access. 2.1.3 Construction Storage Yard & Contractor Limits: Contractor shall store all equipment and material within the designed laydown yard. Contractors shall restore this area to pre-construction conditions. Regardless of the area, the yard shall be fenced. Contractor shall keep the fence well maintained and the site clean and mowed. Contractor shall obtain approval for any project limits changes prior to construction commencement from 7 CES through the Contracting Officer. The approved laydown yard will be provided at the pre-construction meeting. 2.1.4 Contractor shall provide material submittals for all materials & products used in the project on an AF Form 3000. All PDFs shall be from original electronic documents; no scans allowed due to file size. 2.1.5 Work is located in a restricted area. The contractor shall submit a two-week schedule to the Escort POC at least one week prior to work starting to ensure escorts are assigned. The schedule should include start/end times for each day, crew sizes, and work locations. 3.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR CONTRUCTION: 3.1.1 Structural frames which support the deflecting surface will be of structural shapes, rolled, punches, and prefabricated for bolting together at site. Deflecting surface will be of galvanized corrugated steel with a minimum of 2 oz. zinc coating per Fed. Spec. WW-P-00405. Sheets shall have a section modulus of not less than 0.0163 inches curbed per inch and shall be of corrosion resistant material with yield point in 50,000 psi range. 3.1.2 All bolts subject to blast temperatures shall be of SAE 1038 steel, heat treated. All nuts, except on anchor bolts, shall be made of all-steel, self-locking type. 4.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR ANCHORAGE 4.1.1 Blast Deflectors shall be installed on existing concrete. Existing concrete has a minimum thickness of 16�. Lynnco "Epoxy-Locked" anchors, with Lynnco No. 22 Epoxy Resin were used to lock in place the existing blast deflectors. 5.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR ASSEMBLY: 5.1.1 All components will be assembled by bolting together with flat washers, under heads and nuts. Welding, brazing or burning of holes is not permitted. All nuts and bolts will be tightened to torques specified by manufacturer. 6.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR FINISH: 6.1.1 All bolts, nuts and washers will be cadmium or zinc plated. All structural members, parts, and corrugated metal will be hot dip galvanized with a minimum coating of 2.0 oz. zinc per square foot of surface. Painting of galvanized surfaces is not required, but any galvanized surface badly scratched or marred, will be re-galvanized or otherwise repaired to the satisfaction of the Contracting Officer. 6.1.2 Contractor shall paint the corresponding aircraft parking position number on the front of the blast deflectors. The Contactor shall provide a 2�x2� number sign mounted 15� above the concrete at the midpoint on the backside of the blast deflector. Markings/sign shall follow details 2 and 8 on sheet C2 of the attached drawings. 7.1 BLAST DEFLECTOR ALTERNATIVES: 7.1.1 At the option of the Contracting Officer, and as specified in Paragraph 2, the Contractor may substitute an alternate type of blast deflector, providing that the following information and data is submitted, prior to the time of bid opening and approved in writing. 7.1.2 Contractor will submit for approval a tabulation of results of full-scale instrumented field tests witnessed and certified by an accredited testing laboratory, in which proposed alternate is subject to the intermediate throttle power of similar engines totaling # 30,000 afterburner thrust @ approx. 90 feet distance from the leading edge of the deflector measured along centerline of bast impingement. Tabulation must show the maximum pressure in psi, temperature in degrees F., vibration frequency in CPS, and vibration amplitude in inches, taken at the centerline of blast impingement on deflector. The results of all such readings may not be greater than the readings submitted for the specified deflector, for each corresponding item. 7.1.3 Contractor must submit results of smoke-pot tests behind similar deflectors, demonstrating that smoke and gases are deflected in a vertical direction, with no evidence of smoke dispersal behind deflectors. 7.1.4 Contractor must submit evidence of satisfactory operation for at least two (2) years in actual field service for continued testing of similar aircraft and jet engines. 7.1.5 Contractor must submit detailed design analysis, showing loads and stresses in structural members, deflecting surface and bolted joints, using the maximum pressure measured in Paragraph 7.1.2, as the average pressure for load calculations. Welds subjected to tension or vibration may not be used; all bolts must be heat treated if subjected to blast temperatures. 7.1.6 Because of thermal shock and cavitation effects, which results in cracking and spalling, concrete deflectors may not be used as an alternate. Perforated deflecting surfaces are not acceptable for this use.

The North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) for this procurement is 237990-Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction which has a small business size standard of $45 Million. J066--Azenta NitroStore System PM and Support Services
description: This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice for the notice of intent to award a sole source contract. This is not a solicitation. Regional Procurement Office (RPO) - East intends to negotiate a sole source contract for 3 years (Base Year plus 2 Option Years) with Avidity Science, LLC, located at 819 Bakke Avenue, Waterford, Wisconsin, 53185, for preventative maintenance services for the Joseph Maxwell Cleland Atlanta VA Medical Center. Background: This requirement is for preventative maintenance to support OEM-authorized preventive maintenance, repair services, remote technical support, and critical spare parts support for the Brooks Life Sciences NitroStore automated -80 °C sample storage system (Serial Number: NITRO2012 01) located at the Jamaica Plain Campus (Building 1E). Current services for preventative maintenance, under Contract 36C24E22P0022, expire 12/6/2026. The NitroStore currently stores approximately 2 million VA research biospecimens supporting Cooperative Studies Program (CSP) trials and the Million Veteran Program (MVP). Continuous maintenance is required to protect irreplaceable Veteran biological samples. Azenta US, Inc (formerly Brooks Life Sciences) is the OEM and exclusive provider of all parts, diagnostics, firmware, proprietary software, and technical support for NitroStore systems worldwide and is the only firm capable of providing the supplies and services necessary. Since the intent is to procure this requirement on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted to SAM.gov Contract Opportunities. The applicable NAICS code is 811210, with a $34.0M size standard. The PSC is J066. The authority for this action is RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible source, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Interested persons may contact the Contracting Officer via email at millicent.covert@va.gov regarding this procurement. The determination to conduct a competitive procurement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer.

title: Stage 2 - Sidney Operations Centre Marine Fuel & Docks Replacement, Gulf Islands National Park Reserve
description: Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to replace the existing docks and marine fueling system at the Sidney Operations Centre (SOC), located at 2220 Harbour Road in Sidney, British Columbia, which serves as the primary Parks Canada Agency office and marine operations base for the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. The work includes the removal, disposal, and replacement of the existing docks, pilings, and associated servicing systems. The Contractor will supply and install new aluminum-frame docks, pilings, water and electrical services, dock lighting, and a new fueling system consisting of a 5,000-litre fuel tank, fuel lines, and dispenser. All in-water works, including the removal of the existing docks and pilings and the installation of the new docks, must be completed within the lower-risk fisheries window between December 1, 2026, and February 15, 2027. Work occurring above the high-water line may be completed outside of this period. The Contractor will be required to implement the mitigation measures identified in Parks Canada Agency’s Basic Impact Assessment to minimize environmental risks and impacts associated with the project. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

title: Ireland – Recreational, cultural and sporting services – Dublin City Council Contract for Architect Led Integrated Design Team for the Installation of a Pontoon at Islandbridge
description: The stretch of the River Liffey near Islandbridge, is home to over 13 Rowing Clubs – one of which belongs to Dublin City Council. In order to link the eastern length of the Liffey from Islandbridge, the Community, Culture and Local Area Services Department of Dublin City Council has obtained planning permission for an access walkway and pontoon to be constructed on one of the small islands east of the weir. This will allow rowers starting at Islandbridge to have access down to Ringsend and vice versa safely. The project comprises a pontoon with associated walkways to facilitate access to the river for rowing boats and kayaks. The project will provide for a platform that would minimize damage to bankside vegetation when launching and retrieving boats and allow a safe platform for kayakers and boaters to embark and disembark. The Islandbridge location has extensive heritage and ecology. In keeping with this, minimal deviation from the existing design and methodology is required to comply with planning regulations. The works proposed plan to combine the following elements: a) A floating pontoon system within the River Liffey anchored to the existing island shore. b) A new stone and concrete platform built out from the riverbank and connected to the pontoon by a new gangway. c) The removal of vegetation on approach to the pontoon and installation of a new access walkway from the south upper River Liffey at the weir to the new pontoon located north on the lower River Liffey. d) The temporary removal, refurbishment and reinstatement of an existing steel footbridge located on the island. e) The removal of poor existing vegetation, pruning of existing healthy trees and the replanting of 25 new high-quality trees and growing shrubs all native to Ireland. f) Temporary regrading of land during site works for access onto the island. . Please note that this project is subject to funding. For further information please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie Resource ID xxxxxxx – Input when notice created.

Die tatsächlichen während der Vertragslaufzeit erfolgenden Beauftragungen können hinsichtlich der in einem Fachlos enthaltenen Bedarfsmengen der jeweiligen Versorgungsnummern abweichen. Die Obergrenze für den jeweiligen Auftrag bildet in jedem Fall die in dem betreffenden Fachlos zusammengefasste Gesamtmenge (Schätzbedarf + Sicherheitszuschlag). Eine Verpflichtung des AG, Einzelaufträge zu erteilen, wird durch diesen Vertrag nicht begründet. Die Vertragslaufzeit beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung und endet nach 4 Jahren. title: France – Software package and information systems – FOURNITURE D’UNE SOLUTION DE FEEDBACK MANAGEMENT (ENQUETES DE SATISFACTION CLIENTS & NPS) ET PRESTATIONS ASSOCIEES
description: . Les directions des branches Services-Courrier-Colis (BSCC) et Grand Public et Numérique (BGPN) de La Poste, représentant six volets fonctionnels, souhaitent renouveler leur solution de Feedback Management et d'Écoute Client. L'objectif est de se doter d’une solution en mode SaaS pour l'administration et la gestion des enquêtes de satisfaction : - création de l'enquête, - programmation, - routage ... - jusque l'exploitation du verbatim, - la restitution des avis et résultats - et en dernier lieu la possibilité de donner une réponse personnalisée au destinataire de l’enquête. . La solution devra permettre la restitution des résultats à tous les maillons de l'organisation (Siège et Territoires), via une connexion SSO, avec des profils et rôles d’utilisateurs différents. . La solution devra permettre la création de dashboard en autonomie selon le type de profil. Les flux de données proviennent de plusieurs SI internes et externes à La Poste, selon les typologies d'enquêtes. . La solution SaaS devra donc s'interfacer avec d'autres outils de La Poste. Les enquêtes couvrent des prestations de services variées au sein de La Poste pour l'ensemble des Directions citées. Chaque Direction a des besoins spécifiques. . La solution devra se conformer au Règlement Général sur la Protection des Données (RGPD). . Le traitement des données personnelles de La Poste, y compris l’hébergement, la sauvegarde et/ou la consultation devra impérativement être localisé au sein de l'Union Européenne (UE), d’un pays de l’Espace Economique Européen (EEE), d’un pays reconnu comme adéquat par l’Union Européenne.. La solution devra également respecter la Politique de Sécurité des SI du Groupe La Poste (PSSIG).

title: Netherlands – Guidance and counselling services – Uitbesteding Vraagwijzertaken
description: De opdracht betreft de uitvoering van de toegang tot het sociaal domein voor de gemeente West Maas en Waal, uitgevoerd onder de naam VraagWijzer. VraagWijzer vormt de toegangspoort voor inwoners met vragen op het gebied van wonen, welzijn, werk, inkomen en zorg. De werkzaamheden omvatten onder meer het verhelderen van ondersteuningsvragen, het verstrekken van informatie en advies, het onderzoeken van hulpvragen, het inzetten van voorliggende voorzieningen en, waar noodzakelijk, het toeleiden naar geïndiceerde ondersteuning. De gemeente West Maas en Waal is een regiegemeente. De opdrachtnemer is verantwoordelijk voor de operationele uitvoering van de toegangstaken. De aanbestedende dienst blijft verantwoordelijk voor beleidsvorming, kaderstelling en contractsturing. De beoogde ingangsdatum van de overeenkomst is 1 januari 2028. description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE High-Performance Computing Software Development and Technical Services REQUIREMENTS-25-1463-27 This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal or Quotation. It is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract nor will the Government pay for any information provided; no basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result from a response to this Sources Sought Notice or Government use of any information provided. Pursuant to FAR Part 10 (Market Research), the purpose of this notice is to: Determine if sources capable of satisfying the agency's requirements exist. Determine whether the acquisition should utilize any of the small business programs in accordance with FAR Part 19. Pursuant to FAR Part 6 and FAR Part 19, competition and set-aside decisions may be based on the results of this market research. This notice in no way obligates the Government to any further action. Requirement: This notice is issued by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Western Acquisition Division (WAD) and Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory (GFDL) to identify sources capable of providing the following: The GFDL, located on Princeton University's Forrestal Campus, Princeton, NJ, is a NOAA research laboratory in the Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research (OAR). GFDL�s mission is to be a world leader in the development of comprehensive, integrated and unified models of the Earth system comprising the atmosphere, oceans, land, biosphere, cryosphere, and ecosystems; and application of these models for the seamless understanding, predictions and projections of the Earth system, from hours to decades and from global-to-regional spatial scales, accounting for natural variations and forced changes. This procurement is to obtain High-Performance Computing (HPC) software development and technical support services for the GFDL. This support is essential to ensuring that users are provided with the necessary support for the systems, network, and software needed to continue to advance the GFDL and NOAA mission. This effort does not include procuring IT equipment or software, per se, though contract personnel may help define requirements for equipment, software, and services to be acquired by the Government The Statement of Objectives, Performance Work Statements and other supporting documents outline the primary performance-based tasks required to successfully satisfy the need in Management Support Services, Technical Support Services, and Scientific Support Services. The scope of this effort shall encompass all of the task areas described in the Performance Work Statements. See the following documents for further details on this requirement: Attachment 1 - Draft Statement of Objectives - Software Development and Technical Support Attachment 2 - Draft Performance Work Statement - Objective 1: Adaptive Earth System Model Development Attachment 3 - Draft Performance Work Statement - Objective 2: Standardized & Secure Endpoints Attachment 4 - Draft PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT - OBJECTIVE 3: HPC Support & Network Security Attachment 5 - Draft PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT - OBJECTIVE 4: Facilities Management, Maintenance, Project Management, and Ancillary Repairs and Alteration Services Attachment 6 - Draft Exhibit A - NOAA/GFDL Computing and Data Storage Resources Attachment 7 - SOO QUALITY ASSURANCE SURVEILLANCE PLAN Attachment 8 - Resource Only - Current Organization 2026_Rev20260929_positions (This document serves as an informational reference only regarding the current labor breakdown and does not specify the labor mix or positions required for the new requirement.) The period of performance is anticipated to be a one-year base ordering period, with four additional one-year optional ordering periods. title: AFLCMC/HNIT seeks expressions of interest regarding a potential commercial coworking space in the environs of Concord, Massachusetts.
description: The purpose of this request for information is to seek responses from interested vendors regarding a potential short-term commercial coworking space service contract for the Enterprise IT as a Service (EITaaS) program, which the agency anticipates that it may award in the summer of 2027. The projected period of performance start date is August 2, 2027. The agency seeks, in particular, responses from vendors that meet the requirements listed below. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) has been attached to this notice, which provides additional information on the required services. Responses should clearly indicate whether the vendor believes that it can meet all requirements. If it believes that it cannot, the vendor should specifically identify the requirements that it believes it can meet and those that it believes it cannot meet. Where possible, the vendor shall indicate and describe the particular property or properties that it believes would be suited to this contract, and the nature of its interest in that property (if any). The agency anticipates, in accordance with Department of the Air Force (DAF) Contract Policy Memo 24-C-10, that the PSC shall be X1AB (Lease/Rental of Conference Space and Facilities) and the NAICS shall be 531120. Note that this service contract, if awarded, will be in full accordance with the requirements set forth in the memo. Property Management: The contractor shall provide an environment that meets the requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement. It shall be approximately within a 6-mile radius of the Concord Town House, 22 Monument Square, Concord, MA (with the approximate coordinates being 42�27'40.1"N 71�20'55.0"W). (The agency may consider an environment outside of this 6-mile radius if it determines that it is in its best interest to do so.) It shall have roughly 30,000 square feet of office space; it shall contain 190 or more workstations, 6 to 8 private �office pods� or �booths� (each of a size sufficient to accommodate one individual), 4 small collaborative spaces (each of a size sufficient to accommodate up to 6 individuals), a commercial lactation pod, and 6 to 8 meeting rooms, with a personnel range of 151-175 individuals when fully operational, and potentially 176-200 individuals to meet future programmatic demands. It shall have a break area/dining area and a shared kitchen area that meet the requirements specified in the PWS. The parking lot or garage shall have a capacity sufficient for all personnel. Within the coworking space, the contractor shall provide a dedicated, private, exclusive fully enclosed office for the operational use of authorized DAF personnel, which meets the security, structural, and other specifications listed in the PWS. IT Support and Maintenance Services: The vendor shall provide IT support for the coworking space�s workstations and conference equipment. It shall provide on-site technical support staffing. It shall monitor the equipment and the IT infrastructure to ensure that equipment is free from defects, that equipment is operable, and that connectivity is maintained. If the vendor observes any actual or potential information security violations in the course of providing this support, it shall report them to the Government Security Manager. Administrative and Janitorial Services: The vendor shall ensure that restrooms are restocked and maintained, that the shared kitchen and kitchen appliances are maintained, that shared kitchen supplies are restocked (including the restocking of the commercial coffee machine and beverage dispenser), that meeting rooms, open seating areas, and other elements of the coworking space are maintained, shall provide front desk staffing, and shall otherwise administer the coworking space in accordance with commercial practices and with agency-specific needs. Software Licenses, Collaboration Licenses, Network Services, Power/Utility Services, and Commercial Wi-Fi: The contractor shall provide these services in accordance with the PWS. Hardware and Enclosures: The contractor shall install and maintain contractor-owned or contractor-leased hardware and equipment (e.g. printers) and shall install and maintain government-owned hardware and equipment (e.g. large-format displays and computer monitors) in accordance with the PWS. It shall permit the installation of a lockable, ventilated, government-owned IT equipment rack or wall-mounted communications cabinet within the dedicated space. This notice is not a solicitation and does not bind the agency in any way. If the agency opts to post a solicitation, it will only consider those bidders that are actively registered on SAM.gov at the time of issuance of the solicitation. Responses are due by 12:00 PM EDT on October 27, 2026, and should be emailed to Contract Specialist Steven C. Bodnar at steven.bodnar@us.af.mil and Contract Specialist Andrew C. St. Maurice at andrew.st_maurice@us.af.mil.

title: AFLCMC/HNIT seeks expressions of interest regarding a potential commercial coworking space in the environs of Concord, Massachusetts.
description: The purpose of this request for information is to seek responses from interested vendors regarding a potential short-term commercial coworking space service contract for the Enterprise IT as a Service (EITaaS) program, which the agency anticipates that it may award in the summer of 2027. The projected period of performance start date is August 2, 2027. The agency seeks, in particular, responses from vendors that meet the requirements listed below. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) has been attached to this notice, which provides additional information on the required services. Responses should clearly indicate whether the vendor believes that it can meet all requirements. If it believes that it cannot, the vendor should specifically identify the requirements that it believes it can meet and those that it believes it cannot meet. Where possible, the vendor shall indicate and describe the particular property or properties that it believes would be suited to this contract, and the nature of its interest in that property (if any). The agency anticipates, in accordance with Department of the Air Force (DAF) Contract Policy Memo 24-C-10, that the PSC shall be X1AB (Lease/Rental of Conference Space and Facilities) and the NAICS shall be 531120. Note that this service contract, if awarded, will be in full accordance with the requirements set forth in the memo. Property Management: The contractor shall provide an environment that meets the requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement. It shall be approximately within a 6-mile radius of the Concord Town House, 22 Monument Square, Concord, MA (with the approximate coordinates being 42�27'40.1"N 71�20'55.0"W). (The agency may consider an environment outside of this 6-mile radius if it determines that it is in its best interest to do so.) It shall have roughly 30,000 square feet of office space; it shall contain 190 or more workstations, 6 to 8 private �office pods� or �booths� (each of a size sufficient to accommodate one individual), 4 small collaborative spaces (each of a size sufficient to accommodate up to 6 individuals), a commercial lactation pod, and 6 to 8 meeting rooms, with a personnel range of 151-175 individuals when fully operational, and potentially 176-200 individuals to meet future programmatic demands. It shall have a break area/dining area and a shared kitchen area that meet the requirements specified in the PWS. The parking lot or garage shall have a capacity sufficient for all personnel. Within the coworking space, the contractor shall provide a dedicated, private, exclusive fully enclosed office for the operational use of authorized DAF personnel, which meets the security, structural, and other specifications listed in the PWS. IT Support and Maintenance Services: The vendor shall provide IT support for the coworking space�s workstations and conference equipment. It shall provide on-site technical support staffing. It shall monitor the equipment and the IT infrastructure to ensure that equipment is free from defects, that equipment is operable, and that connectivity is maintained. If the vendor observes any actual or potential information security violations in the course of providing this support, it shall report them to the Government Security Manager. Administrative and Janitorial Services: The vendor shall ensure that restrooms are restocked and maintained, that the shared kitchen and kitchen appliances are maintained, that shared kitchen supplies are restocked (including the restocking of the commercial coffee machine and beverage dispenser), that meeting rooms, open seating areas, and other elements of the coworking space are maintained, shall provide front desk staffing, and shall otherwise administer the coworking space in accordance with commercial practices and with agency-specific needs. Software Licenses, Collaboration Licenses, Network Services, Power/Utility Services, and Commercial Wi-Fi: The contractor shall provide these services in accordance with the PWS. Hardware and Enclosures: The contractor shall install and maintain contractor-owned or contractor-leased hardware and equipment (e.g. printers) and shall install and maintain government-owned hardware and equipment (e.g. large-format displays and computer monitors) in accordance with the PWS. It shall permit the installation of a lockable, ventilated, government-owned IT equipment rack or wall-mounted communications cabinet within the dedicated space. This notice is not a solicitation and does not bind the agency in any way. If the agency opts to post a solicitation, it will only consider those bidders that are actively registered on SAM.gov at the time of issuance of the solicitation. Responses are due by 12:00 PM EDT on October 27, 2026, and should be submitted via SAM.gov, rather than via email. If your organization experiences technical issues while attempting to submit via SAM.gov, you may email Contract Specialist Steven C. Bodnar at steven.bodnar@us.af.mil and Contract Specialist Andrew C. St. Maurice at andrew.st_maurice@us.af.mil.

title: Renovate Building 736 Fort Leonard Wood, MO
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District (USACE) is seeking contractors to renovate Building 736 at Fort Leonard Wood, MO. Building 736 is a 40,640 Square Foot (SF), three story, permanent construction barrack facility was built in the 1960s and currently houses basic training/one station unit training (BT/OSUT) trainees. A design was completed by the Kansas City District Corps of Engineers in April 2019 and updated in accordance with UFC changes in June of 2024. This requirement will consist of selective demolition and renovation and modernization of one barracks building and associated sitework at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri. This project includes renovation of a 40,640 SF Barracks Building and construction of an addition of approximately 3,000 SF addition to the building, and associate fine grading, landscaping, and other site work per the plans and specifications provided.

title: Weinfelden and Müllheim Hydropower Plants – General Planning Services
description:
The subject of the procurement is the interdisciplinary general planning services for the further design and implementation of the Weinfelden and Müllheim hydropower plants in the Canton of Thurgau.


The procurement is carried out jointly by Wasserkraftwerke Weinfelden AG, Thurkraftwerk AG and Isento Wasserkraft AG.


The mandate includes, in particular, the construction of the new hydropower plants, the restoration of fish passage, hydraulic engineering works, the dismantling of existing power plants and canal facilities, as well as the restoration of the affected areas and watercourses.


The procurement comprises two project lots:

  • Lot 1 – Weinfelden Hydropower Plant: Contracting authority Wasserkraftwerke Weinfelden AG, general planning services for phases 32–53
  • Lot 2 – Müllheim Hydropower Plant: Contracting authorities Thurkraftwerk AG and Isento Wasserkraft AG, general planning services for phases 31–53


Applications and tenders must cover both project lots. It is intended to award both project lots to the same general planner. A separate general planning contract will be concluded for each project lot.

The corrected attachment is titled "PTAG_ RFI-27-1001_ For awards certificates medallions_FINAL.V2" 4) Added attachment titled "PTAG_ RFI-27-1001_photos of career awards" THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which small business contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified small business contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS 339999 - All Other Miscellaneous Manufacturing and PSC 7690 - Miscellaneous Printed Matter Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) USPTO is seeking a contractor who can fulfill the agency�s requirements for the following awards, certificates, medallions, as well as appropriate packaging and direct shipping for each. This requirement includes manufacturing, assembly and preparing the awards for delivery and shipping directly to the recipient or to an agency office as required. The Office of Human Resource (OHR) supports a variety of non-monetary awards to recognize and reward employee excellence. Superior performance is generally considered as the type of employee performance that contributes, directly or indirectly, to the mission of the USPTO. These non-monetary awards include Bronze Medal Awards, Career Achievement Awards which includes Distinguished Career Awards and Exceptional Career Awards, Retirement Certificates, Directors Award, Length of Service Award and Leadership in Action Award. These awards range in style and type to include framed certificates, medals encased in leucite and presented with a certificate and display box and laser etched clear crystal desktop awards. Note: Sample photos of the awards are attached in a pdf to this RFI 1) Bronze Medal Awards- This award is used to recognize an organization, group or individual employees who have made a major impact on the effectiveness of the USPTO. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity per year is up to 450. 2) Distinguished Career Awards: This award marks at least 20 years of superior performance as an employee of the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 150. 3) Exceptional Career Awards: This award marks at least ten (10) years of superior performance with the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 275. 4) Retirement Certificates: The purpose of this certificate is to recognize USPTO employees upon the occasion of their retirement. These are ordered/requested upon notification of an employee retiring. Framed certificates are created throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 120. 5) Directors Award: The purpose of this award is to recognize individuals and/or group recognition for contributions to the Agency, Managers, supervisors or other employees may nominate those whose contributions have far exceeded expectations or reflect positively on the USPTO. These awards are sporadic throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 100. 6) Leadership in Action Award. The recipients are recognized during the USPTO Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony. The Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity of Leadership in Action awards is up to 400 per year. The three (3) award tiers are Supervisor of the Year (SOTY), Supervisor of the Year (SOTY) Finalist, Approved Nominated Supervisors. Each award tier has a different associated cost and quantity. 7) Length of Service Award: The purpose of this award is to recognized USPTO employee�s length of Federal service. This award is issued monthly. The estimated quantity per year is approximately 2,600. The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the experience and the range of awards and services provided. This will allow USPTO management to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE All interested contractors should provide the following information in their response via e-mail to the contacts listed below: The email subject should include: �RFI-27-1001 Awards fabrication sources sought� Your contractor name, address, SAM UEI, point of contact information, email, phone, website address. Your FSS Schedule contract number (Only if applicable). Any relevant certifications or other relevant authorizations Information about your firm�s ability to meet the requirements stated above Please provide a tailored capability statement addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. Please provide photos and specs of awards your company manufactures consistent with the requirements listed above. A link to award photos on your website will suffice as well. Past Performance � Please provide info on previous government agencies or private businesses you�ve done similar work for in the past. Please include a short description of the work done and photos of the awards provided (if possible) Please include civilian customer/Government Agency contact information including: contact name and organization, telephone number, and email address. QUESTIONS Questions regarding this RFI are due no later than Friday, October 9, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET and are to be submitted via email to roy.pitman@uspto.gov and christopher.ward@uspto.gov NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE DEADLINE: Responses are due no later than Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET and are to be submitted via email to roy.pitman@uspto.gov and christopher.ward@uspto.gov NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE Late responses may be considered at the government�s discretion. Disclaimer: This PTAG Sources Sought Request For Information (RFI) notice is issued solely for Market Research information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled in accordance with procurement integrity requirements. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.

title: Microelectronics Sourcing Capability for Tobyhanna Army Depot (RFI 2)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command (ACC) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as market research to identify qualified Original Component Manufacturers (OCMs) and their Tier-1 direct distributors (directly working with manufacturer) capable of supplying commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS), industrial, and defense-grade microelectronics in sustained, large-scale production volumes for Circuit Card Assembly (CCA) integration. The primary objective is to transition from spot-market, broker-dependent, and decentralized procurement models toward resilient, long-term, direct-tier relationships with primary component fabricators and direct suppliers. The Government seeks insights into volume production capacity, minimum lead times, wafer/die allocations, packaging assurances, and transparent chain-of-custody protocols. Disclaimer: This RFI is published solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. See Attachment 1 - Request for Information for a full description of the Government's requirement for High-Volume Microelectronics Sourcing: Direct Manufacturer & Tier-1 Production Supply Chains.

title: H112--Secutron Fire Alarm testing and Maintenance at the VA Northern California Health Care System (VANCHCS)
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, NCO 21, intends to award a sole source firm fixed price contract to Low Voltage Specialty Inc., for a base year plus four option years, because we believe they are the only authorized company in Northern California to provide Fire Alarm Maintenance and Testing services on the Secutron Fire Alarm Systems. We believe there are no authorized third parties that can provide these Fire Alarm Maintenance and Testing services that can satisfy this requirement. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is attached. If you believe that your company is capable and authorized to perform these services in accordance with the draft PWS, please provide your information and capability along with an authorization letter, by responding to angela.gerlitzki1@va.gov no later than October 27, 2026, by 10 am PST. The applicable NAICS Code is 238210, and the size standard is $19 Million. Product Service Code for this requirement is H112 - Quality Control- Fire Control Equipment. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes. Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: The US Army Corps of Engineers Engineer Research and Development Center ERDC intends to issue an award to BioOne, 21 Dupont Circle, NW STE 800, Washington, D.C. 20036 a sole source basis utilizing Simplified Acquisition Procedures as outlined in FAR Part 12. The requirement is for one physical site licenses for the following journals Subscription Supply from the BioOne. title: USCIS FY27 1st Quarter Engagement with Industry
description: United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), Office of Contracting (OCON), will host its Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 First Quarter Engagement with Industry on October 27, 2026, beginning at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time. These quarterly engagements provide an opportunity for open dialogue between USCIS and industry regarding current and anticipated procurement requirements. The purpose of this event is to share the most current procurement-related information available for USCIS requirements. To participate as an attendee, please self-register using the Microsoft Teams link below: Microsoft Teams meeting https://events.gcc.teams.microsoft.com/event/74f50b56-1413-4370-8199-58b2c86f4a98@5e41ee74-0d2d-4a72-8975-998ce83205eb?source=copyLinkLegacyShareLinkDialog USCIS uses Microsoft Teams to conduct these industry engagements. Attendees will be muted upon entry, and attendee video will be disabled. Only presenters will be on video. USCIS plans to record this event and post the recording on its YouTube channel after the event. Once available, the recording link will be posted as an update to this SAM.gov announcement. USCIS expects to post draft presentation slides to this announcement on or about October 13, 2026. Format and Questions The event will be organized by execution division and then by the Associate Chief portfolio supporting each program office. Presenters will brief the requirements within each portfolio, including new information and updates, as applicable. Following each portfolio briefing, USCIS will address questions related to that portfolio. Attendees may submit questions through the Microsoft Teams Q&A feature or ask questions verbally when the floor is opened for questions. Please include the requirement title and the applicable slide number and/or Acquisition Planning Forecast System (APFS) number, if available. To help USCIS manage the agenda and stay on schedule, USCIS will address only questions related to the portfolio currently being presented. Once USCIS moves to the next portfolio, it will not return to take additional live questions on a prior portfolio. USCIS strongly encourages industry to submit questions in advance. Advance submission allows USCIS to coordinate with the appropriate program and contracting personnel and provide the most accurate and timely information available during the event. Please submit advance questions to USCIS_Vendoroutreach@uscis.dhs.gov no later than 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 20, 2026. USCIS will collect and review questions received during the event. USCIS will post responses to those questions as an update to this announcement. Information posted to SAM.gov after the event will supersede information provided during the live engagement. Disclaimer The information provided during this event and in the accompanying presentation is for planning purposes only. It does not constitute a pre-solicitation notice, invitation for bids, request for proposals, or request for quotations. The Government is under no obligation to purchase products or services discussed unless and until a formal solicitation or invitation for bids is issued and a contract or order is awarded. All planned procurements are subject to change or cancellation. Requirements currently under an active solicitation or source selection will not be further discussed. Questions regarding those requirements should be directed to the designated Contracting Officer. The remaining Fiscal Year 2027 quarterly industry engagement schedule is provided below: 2nd Quarter: January 26, 2027 3rd Quarter: April 27, 2027 4th Quarter: July 27, 2027

title: PTOEA RFI: USPTO seeks a Contractor for Executive Recruitment Services
description: AMENDED TO: 1) Add the answers to questions received by the question deadline 2) Re-open until to 10/27/26 at 1pm to allow for respondents submit a new response or revise their existing submissions THIS IS A PTOEA SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. In accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act (PTOEA), 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A), this Sources Sought Notice Request For Information) (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTOEA The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering by which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will determine which contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, if a solicitation is issued, it will only be issued to the/ those qualified contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS 561312 � Executive Search Services and PSC R431 Support�Professional: Human Resources The purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) Notice 1. Background The USPTO is a federal agency in the Department of Commerce (DOC), which is headquartered in Alexandria, VA. The mission of the USPTO is to foster innovation and competitiveness by providing high quality and timely examination and issuance of patent and trademark applications, guiding domestic and international intellectual property policy, and delivering intellectual property information and education worldwide. Through the issuance of patents, the USPTO encourages technological advancement by providing incentives to invent, invest in, and disclose new technology worldwide. Through the registration of trademarks, the agency assists businesses in protecting their investments, promoting goods and services, and safeguarding consumers against confusion and deception in the marketplace. The office employs over 13,000 full-time staff to support its work. 2. Objectives The USPTO is seeking to establish a single-award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a firm specializing in executive-level recruitment. The ideal partner will possess a proven track record of sourcing high-caliber passive candidates through proprietary networks, global executive databases, and direct headhunting methodologies. The vendor must demonstrate the ability to identify and attract diverse, competitive talent for Senior Executive Service (SES) and Senior Level (SL) equivalent roles, with a specific focus on passive candidates currently employed in top-tier organizations across the following disciplines: Patent, Trademark, Information Technology, Finance, Cyber Security, General Law, and Administrative Services. 3. Abbreviated Scope of Work This effort is for executive search services to identify, deliver and recruit highly qualified candidates for identified USPTO SES and/or SL vacancies and to have those candidates submit applications through USAJobs for the specified vacancies. The contractor shall ensure that all identified candidates possess the required professional, technical and executive core qualifications as outlined in the attached position description associated with each vacancy and as outlined by each specific call order. The contractor shall present a detailed recruitment plan for each specified vacancy, that provides a detailed approach to marketing, searching for candidates, and the process for assisting the candidate with the USAJobs application process.The contractor shall maintain a record of contact/information exchange with all contractors identified candidates and notify the USPTO when their identified candidate(s) have submitted their application to USAJobs. The contractor shall provide weekly status reports to the USPTO outlining progress related to the specified search. 4. Deliverables Deliverables shall carry over to each BPA Call as follows: EVENT 1: Draft Recruitment Plan DELIVERY DATE: Date of Proposal Submission EVENT 2: Kick-Off Meeting DELIVERY DATE: Within five (5) business from award (to be scheduled by the Government) EVENT 3: Final Recruitment Plan DELIVERY DATE: Five (5) days after Kick-off Meeting EVENT 4: Application Notification DELIVERY DATE: Within 2 business days of applicant submitting via USAJobs, as applicable 4. Special Requirements For the applicants to be considered for the position, their application package must be successfully uploaded to the USAJobs.gov website, unless otherwise specified by the specific call order. Applications must meet the requirements that will be stated in the vacancy announcement by the closing date of the posting. 5. Place of Performance a) This work will be performed via virtual recruitment and/or at the contractor�s offsite location. b) All work related to this contract shall be performed in the United States (U.S.) and legally authorized U.S. territories (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands), at either the USPTO�s campus in Alexandria, Virginia, the Contractors� and subcontractors� facilities authorized in the USPTO granted Authorization to Operate (ATO), and/or from USPTO approved telework locations. Work at any other location is prohibited unless authorized by the Contracting Officer. This shall be construed to include all means of telecommunication access to the ATO system and supporting infrastructure as well. c) Any work authorized pursuant to this contract under a telework provision, for any reason, is subject to the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) approval. The following additional requirements must also be met: All authorized telework shall be conducted solely on USPTO authorized systems, devices, and baseline configurations over USPTO approved remote access systems and access technologies. All authorized telework shall only access USPTO and/or Contractor networks and systems within the system boundary from the approved telework location set forth in the Telework Agreement. All authorized telework shall only access USPTO and/or Contractor networks and system via connection authorized by the USPTO granted ATO. No data shall be transferred for ANY reasons to systems and/or devices outside of the authorized secure system boundary of the USPTO granted ATO. The Contractor shall be responsible for any costs/expenses associated in making its staff telework ready. At no time shall any USPTO provided equipment be permitted outside of the U.S. and legally authorized U.S. territories. 6. Estimated Period of Performance The USPTO anticipates awarding a BPA with a Base year + 4 Option Years. 7. Estimated Volume The USPTO anticipates multiple executive searches annually, but an estimated number of searches is not available at this time. The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the experience and the range of executive services provided. This will allow USPTO management to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. description: CGC MANTA � FUEL TANK CLEANING This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. title: FAA Flight Program Operations Support for Organization Designation Authorization (ODA)
description: Introduction: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is seeking input from industry participants regarding the transition of its current Time and Materials (T&M) contract for Flight Program Operations support to a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. This market survey aims to gather information that will assist the FAA in understanding the requirements and potential challenges associated with this transition. All attachments and information herein are subject to change if/when an official solicitation is released. Background: The FAA Flight Program Operations performs multiple missions requiring airborne operations, including Aviation Safety Training, Flight Inspection, Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, and Critical Event Response/Transportation. The current contract provides engineering, certification, Organization Designation Authorization (ODA), and project management services for aircraft modification, certification, continued operational airworthiness, and fleet modernization activities. This will be a follow-on requirement to FAA contract 6973GH-22-D-00031. The incumbent is Delta Engineering Corporation (SAM UEI: MJNYMCPK6M18). The preponderance of work under this contract is performed under a Labor Hour (LH) contract type. Objective: The objective of this RFI is to collect information from interested and capable vendors on the necessary data, methodologies, and considerations for transitioning the existing Labor Hour (LH) contract to a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) structure in compliance with recently updated agency acqusition policies and procedures. The procurement strategy, award methodology, and nature of competition for this requirement has not yet been determined. Responses to this announcement may be used to finalize draft requirement information, inform the development of a future solicitation, and/or to determine the FAA's procurement strategy whether to conduct an open and unrestricted competition, or set-aside this procurement, in part or in whole, to small business concerns. If interested in submitting a proposal for any resulting solicitation for this work, please make the FAA aware of your company's capability and interest by responding to this announcement. Preliminary Workload and Staffing Assumptions: For planning purposes, the FAA estimates an annual baseline of 4.0 Full-Time Equivalents (FTE) or 7,520 labor hours. The breakdown is as follows: Labor Category FTE Annual Hours ODA Administrator 1.0 1,880 Engineering / Flight Test ODA Unit Members 2.0 3,760 Project Manager 1.0 1,880 Total 4.0 7,520 The 2.0 FTE / 3,760 hours for Engineering/Flight Test ODA Unit Members represents an aggregate technical level of effort. It is not intended to require two specific individuals. The Contractor should provide the appropriate number and mix of qualified Unit Members and Flight Test ODA personnel based on the disciplines and requirements of each project. Estimated Workload: Concurrent active projects: 4�8 New STCs: 2�4 STC amendments: 4�8 Other certification/engineering actions: 10�20 Over and Above (O&A) actions: 5�10 Conformity/TIA/flight-test activities: As required by STC/STC amendment workload Conformity, TIA, and flight-test activities are currently workload-driven activities associated with individual STCs and STC amendments. The level of effort for future activities will likely vary based on the scope and certification requirements of each project. Flight Program Operations considers 4.0 FTE / 7,520 annual labor hours to be a reasonable preliminary baseline for market research and Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) purposes. Vendor Statement of Interest and Capabilities: The FAA requests the following information from interested and capable vendors: FIRST - An introduction/overall capabilities statement of your company SECOND - System for Award Management (SAM) Unique ID THIRD - Recommended NAICS for this type of work FOURTH - Descriptions of current relevant certifications possessed by your company. FIFTH - Small Business Status; please define your small business status (8(a), Woman-owned, Veteran-owned, etc.) SIXTH - An authorized point of contact, to include: name, title, telephone number, business address, and email address Request for Information (RFI): The FAA invites responses to the following questions: 1. What are the main factors that should be considered when transitioning from a Cost-type contract to an FFP contract for services related to aircraft modification and certification? 2. How should the FAA address risks and uncertainties inherent in an FFP contract structure for this type of work? 3. What specific information would industry require from the FAA to accurately propose a Firm Fixed Price for the scope of work described in the Performance Work Statement (PWS)? 4. What are the critical data points and historical performance metrics necessary to establish a realistic and competitive fixed price? 5. Please provide insight into a FFP pricing structure that makes sense for this type of work with Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) information for the FAA�s budgetary planning purposes. This will information not be considered by the FAA to be official proposal information; however, please mark any such competitive or sensitive information appropriately. Submission Instructions Interested vendors must provide responses via email. Responses must be in common electronic writable formats such as Microsoft Word, Excel, and/or PowerPoint. Adobe PDF documents. All responses, submittals, and any questions for this Market Survey must be e-mailed to the Contracting Officer, Josh Huckeby, at joshua.d.huckeby@faa.gov on or before the closing date of this announcement. Please include �MARKET SURVEY RESPONSE: ODA STC_(Your Company Name)� in the subject line of your email. Information provided will not be released but please mark PROPRIETARY on all documents submitted as appropriate. Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management at (www.SAM.gov) to be eligible for award of any future FAA contracts for this requirement. Disclaimer: A Screening Information Request (SIR)/Request for Offer may be made under a separate announcement in the future. The FAA is not seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals. The FAA will not pay for any information received or costs incurred in preparing vendor responses to this market survey. Therefore, any cost associated with a market survey submission is solely at the interested vendor expense. The FAA�s acquisition regulation is the Acquisition Management System (AMS). Our agency is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). You can learn more about FAA acquisition policy and procedures at the following website: https://fast.faa.gov/PPG_Procurement.cfm
