title: USCIS FY27 1st Quarter Engagement with Industry
description: United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), Office of Contracting (OCON), will host its Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 First Quarter Engagement with Industry on October 27, 2026, beginning at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time. These quarterly engagements provide an opportunity for open dialogue between USCIS and industry regarding current and anticipated procurement requirements. The purpose of this event is to share the most current procurement-related information available for USCIS requirements. To participate as an attendee, please self-register using the Microsoft Teams link below: Microsoft Teams meeting https://events.gcc.teams.microsoft.com/event/74f50b56-1413-4370-8199-58b2c86f4a98@5e41ee74-0d2d-4a72-8975-998ce83205eb?source=copyLinkLegacyShareLinkDialog USCIS uses Microsoft Teams to conduct these industry engagements. Attendees will be muted upon entry, and attendee video will be disabled. Only presenters will be on video. USCIS plans to record this event and post the recording on its YouTube channel after the event. Once available, the recording link will be posted as an update to this SAM.gov announcement. USCIS expects to post draft presentation slides to this announcement on or about October 13, 2026. Format and Questions The event will be organized by execution division and then by the Associate Chief portfolio supporting each program office. Presenters will brief the requirements within each portfolio, including new information and updates, as applicable. Following each portfolio briefing, USCIS will address questions related to that portfolio. Attendees may submit questions through the Microsoft Teams Q&A feature or ask questions verbally when the floor is opened for questions. Please include the requirement title and the applicable slide number and/or Acquisition Planning Forecast System (APFS) number, if available. To help USCIS manage the agenda and stay on schedule, USCIS will address only questions related to the portfolio currently being presented. Once USCIS moves to the next portfolio, it will not return to take additional live questions on a prior portfolio. USCIS strongly encourages industry to submit questions in advance. Advance submission allows USCIS to coordinate with the appropriate program and contracting personnel and provide the most accurate and timely information available during the event. Please submit advance questions to USCIS_Vendoroutreach@uscis.dhs.gov no later than 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 20, 2026. USCIS will collect and review questions received during the event. USCIS will post responses to those questions as an update to this announcement. Information posted to SAM.gov after the event will supersede information provided during the live engagement. Disclaimer The information provided during this event and in the accompanying presentation is for planning purposes only. It does not constitute a pre-solicitation notice, invitation for bids, request for proposals, or request for quotations. The Government is under no obligation to purchase products or services discussed unless and until a formal solicitation or invitation for bids is issued and a contract or order is awarded. All planned procurements are subject to change or cancellation. Requirements currently under an active solicitation or source selection will not be further discussed. Questions regarding those requirements should be directed to the designated Contracting Officer. The remaining Fiscal Year 2027 quarterly industry engagement schedule is provided below: 2nd Quarter: January 26, 2027 3rd Quarter: April 27, 2027 4th Quarter: July 27, 2027

title: LOC Novel High-Density Optical Data Storage
description: The Library of Congress, hereinafter referred to as the �Library� or �LOC�,� is exploring innovative preservation methods for its digital collections. The LOC is seeking to determine the feasibility of utilizing ultra-high density optical data storage designed for the long-term preservation of a subset of the Library�s digital collections. Currently, the Library manages over 1 billion unique objects of digital preservation data (~33 petabytes) via traditional storage methods. For longevity and reduced migration intervals, it may be reasonable for this portion of data to be permanently stored on a novel medium. The focus would be on a solution that exhibits high areal density, a long lifespan, reduced maintenance/migration cycles, is immutable, and displays a high level of durability. The Library aims to demonstrate the feasibility of an innovative optical data storage solution as a high-density, scalable, and durable medium for storing its preservation collection. The Library wishes to examine the feasibility of this method on a small subset of its digital collections. To be successful, a variety of data formats�including video, audio, text, and images� must be encoded onto the media, errors must be detected/recorded, preservation techniques must be validated and select data must be recalled/read with high fidelity. This work will contribute to the boundary pushing field of high-density optical data storage while pushing the boundaries of access and preservation. The desired outcomes of this requirement are as follows: The successful writing of 1TB of the Library�s digital data in various formats (video, audio, images, text) onto a robust high-density optical media designed to outlast legacy storage solutions at a higher areal density. The determination of the accuracy of the writing process by demonstrating early-stage error detection and ultimate 100% recovery of data. The documentation of successful processes, shortcomings, error rates, timelines, potential solutions to issues, risks, trends, and technological improvements throughout the period of performance as they pertain to the media of choice. Proof of concept for the potential indefinite storage approach of the Library�s data on a novel optical storage medium. The successful recall and reading of all Library-furnished digital files that have been encoded on the media of choice. The isolation of a subset of the data will be carefully curated and stored for the purposes of an educational and artistic display. This will used for educational and display purposes for Library visitors.

title: ILS Maintenance
description: This public posting is for informational, planning, and market research purposes only and constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) and a Sources Sought Request (SSR) only for United States, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP). This announcement does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise that a solicitation or procurement will be issued. This is not a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bids (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. No questions will be addressed at this time. As a component of the United States (U.S.) Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is responsible for protecting our Nation�s borders in order to prevent terrorists and terrorist weapons from entering the U.S. while facilitating the flow of legitimate trade and travel. CBP is also responsible for apprehending individuals attempting to enter the U.S. illegally; stemming the flow of drugs and other contraband; protecting our agricultural and economic interests from harmful pests and diseases; protecting American business from theft of their intellectual property; and regulating and facilitating international trade, collecting import duties, and enforcing U.S. trade laws. In support of this responsibility CBP has implemented and deployed numerous technology systems across the U.S. and internationally that require systems administration and maintenance services. ILD manages a 24/7 Maintenance Dispatch Center for maintenance activities. The Maintenance Dispatch Center (MDC) initially responds to service calls from the numerous CBP sites. The Maintenance Dispatch Center staff record the calls for service in the CBP databases ServiceNow and Integrated Logistics Support System, i.e., MAXIMO). Maintenance Dispatch Center staff issue requests for repair or maintenance services to the Contractor in the form of a Work Order (WO) that initiates the maintenance request. The Contractor responds to the CBP sites, effects repair or completes maintenance actions, and provides periodic status updates and Work Completion Forms (WCF) to the Maintenance Dispatch Center based on the provided requirements contained in this Performance Work Statement.

title: LOC Novel High-Density Optical Data Storage
description: 10/15/2026 AMENDMENT 0001 The purpose of this solicitation amendment is to provide Amendment 0001 and all related updated solicitation attachments, which will provide responess to all questions submitted timely to the Library of Congress by interested parties and potential offerors. All other solicitation terms and conditions remain unchanged. ************************************************************************************************************************************************** The Library of Congress, hereinafter referred to as the �Library� or �LOC�,� is exploring innovative preservation methods for its digital collections. The LOC is seeking to determine the feasibility of utilizing ultra-high density optical data storage designed for the long-term preservation of a subset of the Library�s digital collections. Currently, the Library manages over 1 billion unique objects of digital preservation data (~33 petabytes) via traditional storage methods. For longevity and reduced migration intervals, it may be reasonable for this portion of data to be permanently stored on a novel medium. The focus would be on a solution that exhibits high areal density, a long lifespan, reduced maintenance/migration cycles, is immutable, and displays a high level of durability. The Library aims to demonstrate the feasibility of an innovative optical data storage solution as a high-density, scalable, and durable medium for storing its preservation collection. The Library wishes to examine the feasibility of this method on a small subset of its digital collections. To be successful, a variety of data formats�including video, audio, text, and images� must be encoded onto the media, errors must be detected/recorded, preservation techniques must be validated and select data must be recalled/read with high fidelity. This work will contribute to the boundary pushing field of high-density optical data storage while pushing the boundaries of access and preservation. The desired outcomes of this requirement are as follows: The successful writing of 1TB of the Library�s digital data in various formats (video, audio, images, text) onto a robust high-density optical media designed to outlast legacy storage solutions at a higher areal density. The determination of the accuracy of the writing process by demonstrating early-stage error detection and ultimate 100% recovery of data. The documentation of successful processes, shortcomings, error rates, timelines, potential solutions to issues, risks, trends, and technological improvements throughout the period of performance as they pertain to the media of choice. Proof of concept for the potential indefinite storage approach of the Library�s data on a novel optical storage medium. The successful recall and reading of all Library-furnished digital files that have been encoded on the media of choice. The isolation of a subset of the data will be carefully curated and stored for the purposes of an educational and artistic display. This will used for educational and display purposes for Library visitors.

title: ILS Maintenance
description: This public posting is for informational, planning, and market research purposes only and constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) and a Sources Sought Request (SSR) only for United States, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP). This announcement does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise that a solicitation or procurement will be issued. This is not a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Invitation for Bids (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. No questions will be addressed at this time. As a component of the United States (U.S.) Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is responsible for protecting our Nation�s borders in order to prevent terrorists and terrorist weapons from entering the U.S. while facilitating the flow of legitimate trade and travel. CBP is also responsible for apprehending individuals attempting to enter the U.S. illegally; stemming the flow of drugs and other contraband; protecting our agricultural and economic interests from harmful pests and diseases; protecting American business from theft of their intellectual property; and regulating and facilitating international trade, collecting import duties, and enforcing U.S. trade laws. In support of this responsibility CBP has implemented and deployed numerous technology systems across the U.S. and internationally that require systems administration and maintenance services. ILD manages a 24/7 Maintenance Dispatch Center for maintenance activities. The Maintenance Dispatch Center (MDC) initially responds to service calls from the numerous CBP sites. The Maintenance Dispatch Center staff record the calls for service in the CBP databases ServiceNow and Integrated Logistics Support System, i.e., MAXIMO). Maintenance Dispatch Center staff issue requests for repair or maintenance services to the Contractor in the form of a Work Order (WO) that initiates the maintenance request. The Contractor responds to the CBP sites, effects repair or completes maintenance actions, and provides periodic status updates and Work Completion Forms (WCF) to the Maintenance Dispatch Center based on the provided requirements contained in this Performance Work Statement.

title: Grand Island Mitigation Site
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Project Description: Grand Island Mitigation Project Anticipated Posting Date: 09 October 2026 Sources Sought Number: W9123827X1CQX SAM Posting Title: USACE SPK DBB Construction � Grand Island Mitigation Project � Sacramento, California SAM Posting Description: This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes to determine the availability, capability, and interest of small business firms for a potential Government requirement. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE; requests for a solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. GENERAL SCOPE: The Sacramento River Grand Island Mitigation Project is a restoration initiative on a 233-acre site located at the western tip of Grand Island in Sacramento County, California, situated at the confluence of the Sacramento River, Steamboat Slough, and Cache Slough. The project is designed to create and enhance approximately 84 acres of self-sustaining aquatic and riparian habitat as compensatory mitigation for the American River Common Features (ARCF) project. The construction scope entails approximately 108,000 cubic yards of total excavation to establish a tidal channel network and create an interior "habitat bowl" with islands and peninsulas, alongside breaching an existing berm to connect the site to Steamboat Slough. Excavated material will be utilized to construct on-site features such as the islands and peninsulas, while the remaining excess material will initially be placed in designated uncompacted fill areas on the island and, if settlement issues arise, hauled off-site by barge. To support the federally listed Western, Yellow-Billed Cuckoo, the revegetation plan establishes a continuous riparian corridor by planting water-tolerant trees and shrubs at lower elevations, transitioning to diverse, later-successional trees and native grasses at higher elevations. Project features also include protecting the Valley Elderberry Longhorn Beetle by transplanting impacted elderberry shrubs to designated on-site areas, followed by irrigation and maintenance of these transplants for the duration of this contract. To stabilize the breach, the design utilizes a hybrid bioengineered approach featuring a quarry stone riprap toe from the channel inverted up to 4 feet, transitioning to a bioengineered slope reinforced with erosion control fabrics and live willow cuttings above. Construction scheduling is subject to strict environmental windows, requiring all in-water work (such as activities in Steamboat Slough) to occur strictly between July 1st and October 31st. To isolate the breach work area from the active waterway during in-water construction, a temporary 250-foot-long steel sheet pile cofferdam must be installed and then fully removed upon project completion. The potential requirement may result in a firm-fixed-price solicitation issued approximately late November 2026. If solicited, the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by mid-March 2027. The Government estimates that construction of the potential requirement can be completed within six hundred and sixty-five (665) calendar days from receipt of Notice to Proceed. If market conditions indicate this estimate may be unrealistic, respondents are encouraged to provide specific information (such as known equipment lead times or other timeline concerns) for Government consideration when responding to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government currently estimates the magnitude of construction for the potential project is between $15,000,000 and $20,000,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for the potential requirement is anticipated to be 562910, Remediation Services. The small business size standard for the NAICS, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $25,500,000 annual revenue. The Product Service Code for the potential requirement is anticipated to be Y1KZ, Construction of Other Conservation and Development Facilities. If there is a reasonable expectation that at least two (2) responsible small business concerns under this NAICS can provide the anticipated services at fair market prices, the Contracting Officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. If competition is set-aside for small businesses, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, requires that the Prime Contractor will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. If no set aside is made, the requirement is competed with full and open competition, and the awarded Contractor is not a small business, the Contractor will be required to self-perform the percent of work identified in the solicitation under FAR 52.236-1, Performance of Work by the Contractor. Contractors with the skill, capabilities, workload capacity, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the project described above (either through self-performance and/or Subcontractor management) are invited to provide capability statements to the primary point of contact listed below. Other than small businesses are also encouraged to submit Capability Statements. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11 inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide the following information: 1) Company name, System for Award Management Unique Entity Identification number (SAM UEID) or Employer Identification Number (EIN), address, point of contact name, contact phone number, contact e-mail address, and statement identifying whether the company employs union or non-union workers. 2) Experience and capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past six (6) years. Developing data-remediation rules, workflows, quality-acceptance criteria, and automated processes. Mapping legacy data structures and formats to a unified EMS data standard.
